sections.chapter_title: Ethernet (ETH): media access control (MAC) with DMA controller
sections.text_helper: Section 48.9.5 "Stopping and starting transmission" in chapter 48 (Ethernet (ETH): media access control (MAC) with DMA controller), RM0522 Rev 1, page 2237.
sections.section_content:
Complete the following steps to pause the transmission for some time:
1. Disable the Transmit DMA (if applicable) by clearing Bit 0 (ST) of ETH_DMAC0TXCR
register (see Channel 0 transmit control register (ETH_DMAC0TXCR)).
2. Wait for any previous frame transmissions to complete. You can check this by reading
the appropriate bits of Tx queue 0 debug register (ETH_MTLTXQ0DR) (TRCSTS[1:0]
is not 01 and TXQSTS=0).
3. Disable the MAC transmitter and MAC receiver by clearing RE and TE bits of the
Operating mode configuration register (ETH_MACCR) Register.
4. Disable the Receive DMA (if applicable), after making sure that the data in the Rx FIFO
is transferred to the system memory (by reading the appropriate bits of Tx queue 0
debug register (ETH_MTLTXQ0DR), PRXQ=0 and RXQSTS[1:0]=00).
5. Make sure that both Tx queue and Rx queue are empty (TXQSTS is 0 in Tx queue 0
debug register (ETH_MTLTXQ0DR) and RXQSTS[1:0] is set to 00.
6. To restart the operation, first start the DMAs, and then enable the MAC transmitter and
receiver.
Note: Do not change the configuration (such as duplex mode, speed, port, or loopback) when the
MAC is actively transmitting or receiving. These parameters are changed by software only
when the MAC transmitter and receiver are not active.
Similarly, do not change the DMA-related configuration when transmit and receive DMA are
active.
